heroHeadline: 14 Days to Kickoff — Iran Demands Multiple-Entry US Visas; UCL Final (May 30) Puts World Cup Players at Risk; Argentina Squad Due in 48 Hours
heroSubtitle: Iran's football federation president Mehdi Taj issued an urgent demand on May 28 that the United States issue multiple-entry visas to the entire Iranian delegation — players, coaches, and medical staff — who must repeatedly cross the US-Mexico border from their Tijuana base camp to reach match venues in Los Angeles and Seattle. No visas have been issued as of today, despite FIFA president Infantino's earlier pledge. Iran faces the Gambia in a warm-up on May 29 in Antalya before the June 1 squad submission deadline. With the UEFA Champions League Final (PSG vs Arsenal) set for May 30 in Budapest, Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi has returned to full PSG training after a thigh scare, but will have virtually zero recovery time before the World Cup — Morocco open vs Brazil at MetLife on June 13. Neymar cleared his calf oedema scare and joined Brazil's camp for their May 31 farewell friendly vs Panama at the Maracanã. Argentina's final 26-man squad — expected to feature 38-year-old Lionel Messi — is due in 48 hours (May 30 deadline), with FIFA publishing all 48 rosters on June 2. Across the tournament, all squad deadlines converge in the next 72 hours: the world will know its complete field on June 2, just nine days before Mexico's Estadio Azteca hosts the tournament opener.
